Article Title: CEA bats for E10 fuel; not feasibile, say officials
Article Text:
Officials were taken aback by the Chief Economic Adviser's comments regarding the availability of E10 fuel

NEW DELHI: An opinion piece by chief economic adviser (CEA) V Anantha Nageswaran on ethanol blending has rekindled the debate whether govt should look at making E10 (10% ethanol blended petrol) available for older vehicles manufactured before April 2023.Officials, dealing with the issue and countering the narrative against E20 fuel for the past few weeks, admitted that the CEA’s views came as a surprise for them as it bats for making E10 available as an option at fuel stations. This is likely to push the demand for making lower-blend of fuel available in addition to E20, they said, adding it won’t be easy logistically and considering that an ecosystem has been in place for 20% of blending that’s linked to the rural economy.TOI has learnt that as of now, there is no discussion within govt to provide the option of E10 at fuel stations. While there has been a campaign demanding petrol with lower ethanol content, a govt official said there was no discussion so far on reverting to fuel with 10% blending. The official said creating additional infrastructure to dispense E10 petrol is not only logistically difficult, but may also lead to practical issues such as pricing and distribution. “Also, allowing the sale of E10 would mean govt is accepting E20 petrol is not good for older vehicles which is not the case. Studies have shown E20 does not cause any mechanical issues,” said another official.
Article Summary: Officials were taken aback by the chief economic adviser's comments regarding the availability of e10 fuel. As of now, there is no discussion within govt to provide the option of e 10 at fuel stations. While there has been a campaign demanding petrol with lower ethanol content, a govt official said there was no discussion so far on reverting to fuel with 10%.

Article Title: 'Follow law of land': Centre to X after Musk announces greater visibility on govt censorship
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Centre on Monday said that Elon Musk-owned X will have to "follow the law of the land" after the social media platform introduced a new rule to make government-driven restrictions on content more visible to users."X will have to follow the law of the land," the officer told news agency PTI.In a post on social media platform X, Musk said that any censorship required by governments is now clearly visible, signalling the platform's intention to provide users with greater insight into actions taken at the request of government authorities."Any censorship required by governments is now clearly visible," Musk said.Under the proposed changes, X users will be able to see when governments seek the removal of posts or request restrictions on accounts.The platform also plans to disclose details about the agencies making such requests and, where available, the legal grounds or justification cited for the action.The move is part of Musk's wider push to make the platform's moderation and content-distribution systems more transparent.Since acquiring X, formerly known as Twitter, Musk has repeatedly argued that users should have greater visibility into how online content is moderated and ranked.
Article Summary: X users will be able to see when governments seek the removal of posts or request restrictions on accounts. The platform also plans to disclose details about the agencies making such requests and, where available, the legal grounds or justification cited for the action.

Article Title: India at 80: From independence to nation-building
Article Text:
But nation building is not only about what we build. It is also about how we build it.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

We have inherited a remarkable country. Our responsibility is to leave behind an even more remarkable one.

That, to me, is the true meaning of independence.

The article has been contributed by Shapoorji Mistry, Chairman,

Shapoorji Pallonji Group

Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of HT Digital by Times Internet’s Spotlight team.

As India celebrated its 80th Independence Day, I was filled with a profound sense of pride. Not only in the India we inherited, but in the India we have the privilege and responsibility to build.For me, the Tiranga represents far more than a national flag. It is a symbol of a civilisation that has endured, evolved and renewed itself across centuries. It speaks of courage and sacrifice, of truth and resilience, and above all, of an unwavering faith in the future.The country's greatest strength has never been simply the antiquity of its civilisation, but it is our extraordinary ability to absorb change without losing ourselves; to embrace knowledge without abandoning wisdom; and to use technology and progress to carry our timeless values into a new age.This year, as India celebrated its 80th Independence Day, the country stood at an important moment in its journey.In a world marked by geopolitical uncertainty, economic fragmentation and extraordinary technological change, India is increasingly being looked upon with confidence and respect. This transformation is a reflection of the aspiration, energy and self-belief of 1.4 billion Indians, strengthened by the decisive leadership and vision of our Prime Minister.His vision of Viksit Bharat is not merely an economic ambition. It is a national calling: an India that is prosperous yet compassionate, technologically advanced yet culturally rooted, strong yet peaceful, confident yet humble. It is a vision that challenges all of us to think beyond the present and take responsibility for the India we wish to leave behind.The responsibility for achieving that India belongs to all of us.As an industry, we have a particularly important role to play. We must invest with conviction, innovate relentlessly, create meaningful employment, build world class infrastructure, nurture talent and develop capabilities that strengthen India's economic and strategic self-reliance.With integrity. With responsibility. With respect for our people and our environment. And with the understanding that the success of an enterprise ultimately has meaning only when it contributes to the progress of the society around it.India's next chapter will be written through a partnership between government, enterprise and society. It will require the energy of our youth, the wisdom of experience, the courage to innovate and, above all, a shared belief that our best years are still ahead of us.Our independence gave us the right to dream, the opportunity to shape our destiny. Now, our generation has the responsibility to make that dream extraordinary.As we reflected on the significance of the Tiranga this Independence Day, let us renew that commitment: to build an India that is brighter, greener, more innovative, more inclusive and more confident. An India that our children will be proud to inherit. And an India that the world will be proud to call its partner.
Article Summary: Shapoorji mistry: we have inherited a remarkable country. Our responsibility is to leave behind an even more remarkable one. The tiranga represents far more than a national flag. It is a symbol of a civilisation that has endured, evolved and renewed itself across centuries.

Article Title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes a 'vacation request' to employees for this August
Article Text:
Julie Sweet asks employees to help deliver a strong fourth quarter

Why Accenture changed its vacation policy

AI remains a key concern for Accenture investors

Accenture CEO Julie Sweet is asking employees to think twice before taking time off this August as the company pushes for a strong finish to its financial year. In a rare one-time policy change, Accenture will allow staff to carry forward any unused vacation days into the next fiscal year instead of requiring them to use the leave before August ends. The move comes alongside Julie Sweet's call for employees to focus on winning new business and generating more revenue in the final weeks of the quarter after the consulting giant reported weaker-than-expected quarterly results. Accenture’s new policy will give its workers more flexibility while helping keep more employees available during the company's year-end sales push.In a memo seen by Bloomberg, Accenture CEO Sweet urged employees to contribute to improving fourth-quarter results by finding new ways to serve clients and generate revenue. "Our shareholders are counting on us to deliver a strong quarter in Q4 — everyone can contribute," Sweet wrote.“This means we all need to find more ways to serve clients that create more revenue in the quarter and to originate more sales (small, large, mega) to finish strong,” she added.According to Bloomberg, the company has also allowed employees to carry over unused vacation days into the next financial year, which begins on September 1.Normally, staff must use their vacation before the fiscal year ends.People familiar with the matter told the publication that the temporary policy change is part of the company's effort to keep more employees working during August rather than taking leave before their vacation days expire. Another person familiar with the matter said the one-time change is also meant to give employees greater flexibility.The move comes after weaker-than-expected results. Accenture reported a 2% decline in new bookings for the quarter ended May 31 and projected fourth-quarter revenue of $17.75 billion to $18.4 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $18.47 billion. Following the earnings announcement in June, Accenture shares fell about 20% in one day, one of the company's biggest single-day declines on record.The earnings report also intensified concerns that artificial intelligence could disrupt the consulting industry in the near term, even though Julie Sweet has described AI as a "tailwind" for Accenture's business.Bloomberg Intelligence said in a recent research note: “AI remains the dominant concern for services and consulting. Though management positions Accenture as a long-term AI beneficiary, tangible evidence that AI is accelerating demand is limited.”
Article Summary: Julie sweet asks employees to help deliver a strong fourth quarter for accenture. In a rare one-time policy change, accenture will allow staff to carry forward any unused vacation days into the next fiscal year. The move comes alongside sweet's call for employees to focus on winning new business and generating more revenue.

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham
Article Text:
Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.The appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.
Article Summary: Indian-origin strategist gautam rangarajan appointed as expert adviser on structure and process at 10 downing street. He brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media. Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox: "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with…" - a lesson on humour, perspective and facing hard times with lightness
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox (AP photo)

Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox

"I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor"

Where this quote actually comes from

Why humour matters most during genuinely difficult stretches

How humour actually helps people manage stress

Why laughing at your own mistakes actually matters

Why humour can genuinely strengthen relationships

Michael J. Fox's own perspective on adversity

Why humour is not the same thing as avoiding a real problem

Why being naturally serious is not actually a flaw

Other memorable quotes by Michael J. Fox

"One's dignity may be assaulted, vandalized and cruelly mocked, but it can never be taken away unless it is surrendered."

"I am careful not to confuse excellence with perfection."

"Family is not an important thing. It's everything."

"Acceptance doesn't mean resignation; it means understanding that something is what it is and that there's got to be a way through it."

Why people still find meaning in this quote

Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox , the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.This line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem.It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Life inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.Stress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.One of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Shared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Fox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.There is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Fox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Humour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.
Article Summary: "i think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor" michael j. Fox, actor and parkinson's disease advocate. Not being able to laugh is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life. Michael j. Fox was one of the most recognisable actors of his generation.

Article Title: ChatGPT gave Google 'Code Red’, prompting co-founder Sergey Brin's return; Now OpenAI’s Greg Brockman is facing 'Red Flag'
Article Text:
Greg Brockman goes into ‘founder mode’

OpenAI witnessing a wave of high-profile departures

In December 2022, the meteoric rise of ChatGPT reportedly triggered a “Code Red” inside Google . The situation led co-founder Sergey Brin back into hands-on technical development. Fast forward to August 2026, the tables have turned, presenting OpenAI leadership led by CEO Sam Altman and president Greg Brockman (both cofounders) with what industry analysts are calling a major “red flag” of their own.A wave of high-profile executive departures is shaking the AI company’s front office at a critical juncture, as the artificial intelligence (AI) giant prepares for an anticipated initial public offering ( IPO ) while seeking to validate an $852 billion valuation.Meanwhile, citing sources familiar to the matter, a report by Axios claims that Brockman is getting more involved in the company’s day-to-day operations to contain disruptions. Brockman is said to be meeting with more customers and teams across the company than ever before. Brockman is said to be publicly framing the departures as a change in corporate focus.The latest blow came with the resignation of chief revenue officer Denise Dresser after less than a year at the company. Dresser, a seasoned software executive who previously spent over a decade at Salesforce and Slack, was recruited in December to spearhead OpenAI's enterprise commercial strategy against formidable rivals like Anthropic.Her departure landed just two days after longtime COO and senior executive, Brad Lightcap, announced his own exit after eight years, leaving key corporate divisions in transition. Her profile expanded significantly four months later when she took over operational duties previously handled by Lightcap. However, Dresser's abrupt departure compounds a broader pattern of senior leadership churn.For example, Fidji Simo, the former Instacart CEO stepped away from her high-ranking OpenAI executive role in July to focus on managing a chronic illness. Four other senior leaders, including former VP of Science Kevin Weil and CMO Kate Rouch, left the company in April. The exits arrive only months after OpenAI submitted a confidential IPO draft registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission, raising concerns among private market watchers.“The executives leaving OpenAI ahead of their IPO is a huge red flag,” noted Kevin McCormick, founder of AI startup SignAudit.AI, pointing out that walking away before a liquidity event suggests underlying tensions.“If the executives leaving aren’t being ‘made whole’ by the next company, it’s bad news for OpenAI,” McCormick wrote, as per a report by CNBC.Meanwhile, Dali Rajic – former COO of cybersecurity firm Wiz – joined as chief revenue officer. OpenAI also hired top AI researcher Noam Shazeer from Google in June 2026. He is a co-inventor of the foundational transformer architecture and former co-lead of Google’s Gemini models, and joined OpenAI to head Architecture Research.
Article Summary: A wave of high-profile executive departures is shaking the ai company’s front office at a critical juncture. Chief revenue officer denise dresser resigned after less than a year at the company. The exits arrive only months after openai submitted a confidential ipo draft registration with the securities and exchange commission.

Article Title: ‘10 online shopping platforms that faced most consumer complaints, non-delivery of goods top grievance; Rs 91 crore refunds in one year’
Article Text:
​10 online shopping platforms that faced most consumer complaints

Top 10 E-Commerce Platforms by Grievance Volume

Regulatory crackdown and refunds

How NCH complaint system works

Online shopping giants Flipkart, Amazon and Meesho emerged as the top three platforms facing the highest volume of consumer grievances on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) in 2025, the government informed the Lok Sabha recently. In a written reply to the Parliament, Union Minister of State for Consumer Affairs BL Verma disclosed that Flipkart topped the list with over 1.33 lakh complaints, followed by Amazon with 91,248 and Meesho with 29,284. Quick-commerce and niche retail platforms also featured prominently among the top ten offenders.Operated by the Department of Consumer Affairs, the NCH acts as a single-window pre-litigation website. It currently supports 17 Indian languages and connects consumers with 1,853 partner companies registered under its voluntary "Convergence" initiative. This means that consumers can lodge complaints in 17 languages, including Hindi, English, Kashmiri, Punjabi, Nepali, Gujarati, Marathi, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Maithili, Santhali, Bengali, Odia, Assamese and Manipuri, through the toll-free number 1915.* Flipkart: 1,33,000* Amazon: 91,248* Meesho: 29,284* Myntra: 25,384* Netmeds: 19,895* Zepto: 5,774* Blinkit: 5,102* Naaptol: 4,079* VLE Bazaar: 3,907* Nykaa: 3,405To curb unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) imposed fines on 47 platforms, slapping collective fines totaling approximately Rs 1.12 crore (Rs 1,12,01,500). The minister highlighted significant enforcement outcomes through pre-litigation resolution.The minister said that the NCH facilitated refunds of over Rs 91 crore to consumers between April 25, 2025, and June 30, 2026, of which more than Rs 63 crore pertained to grievances in the e-commerce sector. This was achieved by resolving over 1,47,000 consumer grievances related to refund claims at the pre-litigation stage, he said. A total of 5.11 lakh complaints related to quick commerce were received on the NCH in 2025, all of which were disposed of, the minister added.Non-delivery of products was the single largest category of complaints in 2025, accounting for 79,818 cases. Other frequent complaints included delivery of the wrong product, denial of replacement or refund as per policy, delivery of defective or damaged goods, non-refund of paid amounts, deficiency in services, sale of spurious or counterfeit products, and unauthorised debit of amounts without consumer consent.Consumers can escalate unresolved e-commerce disputes through:* Toll-Free Helpline: 1915* WhatsApp / SMS: 8800001915* Email: nch-ca@gov.in* Complaint websites: consumerhelpline.gov.in, the NCH app, and the UMANG application

Article Title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to AI companies: Fulfil your Cancer promise, rather than blaming me
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei dismissed calls for AI firms to rely on glossy campaigns

A rare, lengthy social media post

What comes next, according to Dario Amodei

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has pushed back against criticism that warnings about AI risks are fuelling public negativity. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Amodei said that the real issue is a ‘crisis of trust’ rooted in decades of suspicion toward companies, governments, and the tech industry. “Ordinary people don’t trust us and suspect we’re cooking up some new way to screw them over,” he wrote.Amodei dismissed calls for AI firms to rely on glossy campaigns to improve their image. “At this point, saying that AI will cure cancer is more a cliché than inspiring,” he said. Instead, he argued that the only way to rebuild trust is to actually deliver breakthroughs like curing cancer, rather than making promises that feel deceptive.Highlighting his own approach, Amodei said he is accountable to biomarkers and adjusts protocols based on measurable outcomes. He compared mastery in diet and health to excellence in academics, sports, or engineering, insisting that self‑control and discipline should be respected as legitimate forms of mastery.“I do agree that the public has a negative view of AI (and that this is a big problem), but I don’t think it is primarily caused by me or any other AI leader warning about AI’s risks.I think it is fundamentally a crisis of trust. I think that ordinary people don’t trust companies, governments, or the tech industry and always suspect that we are cooking up some new way to screw them over. The causes of this go back decades and AI is just the latest iteration of it. I don’t think that a glitzy marketing campaign with a positive spin (which some have advocated that Anthropic do) is the way to win back that trust — at this point, saying that AI will cure cancer is more a cliche than it is inspiring, and most people think it is deceptive. The thing that will work is *actually curing cancer*. I think by far the most accurate criticism of AI companies including Anthropic is that we haven’t yet delivered on our big promises to benefit the world. That is totally on us, and I think it’s the criticism you should be making, instead of all this stuff about messaging and marketing”, wrote Amodei on X.Amodei laid out his argument in an extended post on X on Saturday, a platform he generally avoids, according to a Fortune report. He began by addressing the debate around AI regulation, describing what he sees as a false choice between critics who worry regulation leads to concentrated corporate power and those who argue that widely distributing AI, including through open-weight models, is the better safeguard. Amodei argued that institutions like the court system show power can be decentralized without abandoning oversight, and noted that Anthropic has backed policies that would slow down frontier AI companies like itself while giving smaller competitors more room to operate.He acknowledged that AI does tend to concentrate power structurally, but attributed that tendency to the scaling laws underlying how AI models improve as more computing resources are put into them, rather than to regulation itself. In his view, open-weight models only shift that concentration toward whoever controls the most computing capacity and chips, rather than eliminating it. He said he favors "rules of the road" that address AI's cyber, biological and alignment risks while also institutionally constraining the power of frontier AI companies and leaving room for open-weight models, and voiced support for a FINRA-like regulatory body as well as the Trump administration's approach to AI testing.Amodei said Anthropic is trying to rebuild credibility by producing tangible results, pointing specifically to increased work in biology and medicine, and describing "early glimmers" of what he suggested could eventually be significant breakthroughs. Until there are actual accomplishments to point to, he said the company would avoid making further big promises and instead focus on being transparent about AI's risks in the meantime, arguing that honesty carries no more public credibility risk, and quite possibly less, than an approach that downplays or distracts from risks people already sense are real.
Article Summary: Anthropic ceo dario amodei has pushed back against criticism that warnings about ai risks are fuelling public negativity. ‘ordinary people don’t trust us and suspect we’re cooking up some new way to screw them over,’ he wrote.

Article Title: When 'Godfather of AI' agreed with Elon Musk; said billionaires like him are right about future of work; but there is a big problem and that is...
Article Text:
Geoffrey Hinton says Musk and Gates are right about AI ending jobs, but warns the real problem is nobody left to buy what AI makes.

Why Geoffrey Hinton thinks the trillion-dollar AI spending spree runs on job cuts

AI will create new jobs, but Hinton says nowhere near enough to replace what it kills

Bernie Sanders warns 100 million US jobs face AI automation risk

Geoffrey Hinton and Elon Musk do not usually land on the same side of an argument. But asked whether the tech billionaires forecasting the end of work were being melodramatic, the Nobel laureate widely called the "Godfather of AI" said they were probably right. Musk has said most people won't have to work at all inside two decades. Similarly, Bill Gates has suggested humans may soon not be needed for most things. Hinton, in a discussion with Senator Bernie Sanders last year at Georgetown University, said those predictions are not fringe. They are likely.The catch is everything that follows. Hinton's worry is not that AI is bad technology. It is that the economy sitting underneath it was not built to absorb what is coming. He expects "massive unemployment caused by AI", and he does not think the people writing the cheques have worked through the consequences. His blunt line to Sanders was that if workers stop earning, "there's nobody to buy their products".Follow the money, Hinton argued, and the intent becomes obvious. Somebody has to recover the roughly trillion dollars flowing into data centres and chips, and subscription fees for chatbots won't cover it. The return has to come from selling companies AI that does a worker's job for less. Big Tech, in his reading, is betting squarely on replacement. The financial pressure is real enough: HSBC estimated OpenAI won't turn a profit before 2030 and may need over $207 billion to keep scaling.Hinton also keeps pointing out that this is a design choice, not destiny. AI could do enormous good in healthcare and education. What makes it dangerous is distribution. Musk gets richer, a lot of people lose work, and as Hinton put it, "that's on how we organize society".The standard rebuttal is that every technology shock eventually produces new categories of work. Hinton accepts the first half and rejects the second. Yes, roles like prompt engineer appear. No, he does not believe they arrive in anything like the volume of the jobs being erased. The old escape route mattered: a ditch digger could move to a call centre. Those call centre desks are the ones going first.He is careful about his own confidence, though. Predicting AI, he told Sanders, is like driving in fog, where the next hundred yards are clear and the two hundred yard mark is invisible. A year or two out, he can see. Ten years out, nobody can. At the Ai4 conference in Las Vegas this month, he went further on capability, saying AI could surpass humans at everything within twenty years, and probably a good deal sooner.Sanders has tried to size the damage. An report last year from his office estimated nearly 100 million US jobs are exposed to automation, covering fast food, customer service and manual labour, but also accounting, software development and nursing. Senator Mark Warner has warned recent graduates could face unemployment near 25% within three years.Hinton's fog is still there. The 175,479 tech jobs cut in this year are not, and the names on that list run through Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, and plenty of others.
Article Summary: Geoffrey hinton says musk and gates are right about ai ending jobs. But he warns the real problem is nobody left to buy what ai makes. He expects "massive unemployment caused by ai", and he does not think the people writing the cheques have worked through the consequences.

What Tesla’s biggest investor Ross Gerber said

Apple’s pricing strategy

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.

Article Title: Indian-origin CEO says he starts checking his emails at 4.30 am; 'If you want to work eight-to five...'
Article Text:
​Indian-origin CEO says work-life balance is not possible at the top.

Work-life balance not possible at the top, says CEO

Who is Khozema Shipchandler?

CEO Khozema Shipchandler said he starts checking his emails at 4.30 am that then wraps up his work at 9 pm. There is no day off and the Indian-origin CEO of Twilio runs laps around the house between meetings so that he does not spend all his time sitting as most of the time he's awake, he is working. In an interview with Fortune, he said that wanting work-life balance is awesome but sacrifice is what separates leaders from everyone else. For example, the 51-year-old CEO said he missed many of his son's tennis matches. The price that he paid made him a CFO when he was 31.On checking mails at 4.30 am, Shipchandler said he was always a morning person, and it helped him to remain ahead of others. Coffee, breakfast, browse through news headlines, and then a workout follow. “I do it in that order intentionally so that while I’m working out, I have an opportunity to think through the various things that have happened, through the course of the news, the things that I’ve seen on email and Slack and stuff like that," he said.Shipchandler is at work at 7.30 am which goes on till lunch. After lunch, he always immediately hits the treadmill for 10 minutes of walking so that he doesn’t get an afternoon lull.Then he takes a dinner break at 6.30 pm. Despite his traveling, he maintains the same routine. At 8 pm, he squeezes in another hour of extra work and then goes to sleep at 9.30 pm. On the weekend, he wakes up at 6.30 am and keeps his routine a little relaxed but he still works most Sundays.Shipchandler said he does not think that work-life balance is possible at the top but he insisted that he is not against smart working. “Every one of us has to make certain work-life choices,” he said. “This work-life choice obviously has certain consequences. I wasn’t there for all of my son’s tennis matches.”“If you want to work eight-to-five, coach your kids sports teams, have the evenings for yourself, and maybe another hobby or interest, that’s awesome,” Shipchandler said.He also doesn’t use social media and says that helps keep his focus.Shipchandler said he was built to work hard. “My parents were the classic immigrant success story, and as with many immigrant parents, they wanted their kids to do better than them and to create the opportunities for them,” he said. “They really pushed working hard and playing hard, which, by the way, I do play hard when I’m not working, so that was the goal,” he added.Shipchandler was born in Indiana to Indian parents who were from Mumbai. But his ancestral home is in Bengaluru. Khozema holds a Bachelor of Arts in Biology and English from Indiana University Bloomington. He started his career at GE and rose through the ranks to become the Chief Commercial Officer. After 22 years at GE, he joined Twilio and became the CEO in 2024.
Article Summary: Indian-origin ceo of twilio says work-life balance is not possible at the top. Khozema shipchandler said he starts checking his emails at 4.30 am that then wraps up his work at 9 pm. The 51-year-old ceo said he missed many of his son's tennis matches.

Article Title: Former Swansea City ballboy Charlie Morgan, kicked by Eden Hazard in 2013, set to sell £500 million Au Vodka empire for reported £100 million payout
Article Text:
From being kicked by Eden Hazard as a teenage ballboy in 2013 to building a £500 million vodka empire, Charlie Morgan’s journey has taken a remarkable turn.

From infamous ballboy incident to vodka entrepreneur

Au Vodka sells more than 35,000 bottles a day

Ronaldinho and Floyd Mayweather among celebrity supporters

Eden Hazard and Charlie Morgan reunite

A former Swansea City ballboy who became internationally known after being kicked by Eden Hazard during a controversial football match is now on the verge of a very different kind of headline. Charlie Morgan, 30, is reportedly in talks to sell his premium vodka brand Au Vodka for around £500 million, 13 years after the infamous incident.According to Sky, Morgan and his school friend and business partner Jackson Quinn are negotiating a potential deal with American drinks giant Sazerac Company. If completed at the reported valuation, the founders could each receive around £100 million, while they may also retain roles within the company.Morgan was just 17 when he became involved in one of the most talked-about incidents of the 2012-13 football season.During Swansea City's League Cup semi-final against Chelsea in January 2013, Morgan collected the ball and appeared to deliberately lie on it in an attempt to waste time. Chelsea midfielder Hazard attempted to retrieve it and kicked Morgan, resulting in the Belgian being sent off.The incident generated worldwide debate, with football fans divided over the actions of both Hazard and the teenager.More than a decade later, Morgan has built a business empire of his own. He launched Au Vodka with Quinn in 2015, and the brand has since grown into a major premium spirits business.Au Vodka has reportedly expanded rapidly and now sells more than 35,000 bottles of its premium vodka every day.The brand is headquartered in Swansea, where Morgan and his team recently moved into an extravagant new headquarters designed around Au Vodka's distinctive gold branding.The building features a gold exterior, gold ceiling, gold café and gold signage, matching the company's signature gold bottles.Reflecting on the company's growth in a LinkedIn post, Morgan recalled how the business began in a tiny 250-square-foot office.“We spent four years in our first office which was only 250 sq ft and only just fit myself, Jackson Quinn and Jordan Major (who was just 16 and packing orders!),” he wrote.The company then moved to an industrial unit in Swansea, where it expanded significantly and grew its workforce to 96 people.“Today we’ve moved into our new home - A fully gold HQ which really represents Au and what we stand for,” Morgan added.Au Vodka has attracted backing and attention from several high-profile names, including Brazilian football legend Ronaldinho and former American boxer Floyd Mayweather.The company's decision to remain headquartered in Swansea has also earned praise from supporters, with some applauding Morgan for keeping the business rooted in his home city despite its rapid international growth.Negotiations over the potential acquisition are understood to have been ongoing for several months, with reports suggesting a deal could be close.Sazerac is reportedly looking to expand its presence in the British drinks market. The company is working with law firm Forsey, while Au Vodka is represented by DLA Piper.The remarkable story eventually came full circle when Morgan and Hazard reunited for an Au Vodka promotional campaign in 2024.The former football rivals put their infamous history behind them and appeared together in a photoshoot promoting Morgan's brand. Hazard shared photographs of the pair on social media, including one showing them holding a glass of blue raspberry Au Vodka.“A nice thing about retirement is catching up with old friends. You have come a long way in 11 years my friend @charliem0rgan,” Hazard wrote on X.Another photograph showed the pair looking at a chessboard surrounded by bottles of Au Vodka.More than a decade after becoming famous for an incident on a football pitch, Morgan now finds himself at the centre of a potential £500 million business deal.
Article Summary: Charlie morgan is reportedly in talks to sell his vodka brand au vodka. The 30-year-old became famous after being kicked by eden hazard in 2013. Morgan and business partner jackson quinn are negotiating a potential deal with american drinks giant sazerac company.
